requirements.prompt: Manage cyber risk through the accountable authority.
Assign executive responsibility for cyber security.
Consider risks to other WA entities and share relevant risks with DGov.
Fund and resource continuing policy implementation.
Give the cyber security executive authority to implement the policy.
Provide the executive with the skills and resources needed.
Report implementation progress to the accountable authority.

Make cyber risks visible to decision makers.

Oversee third-party security arrangements.
Maintain plans for implementing the policy.
Plan continuity, incident response and recovery.
Obtain assurance that security controls work, including ACSC controls.

Apply WA information classification when assessing offshore data.
Oversee secure disposal of devices and storage media.

Follow whole-of-government cyber directions or obtain an exemption.
Consider DGov threat intelligence and advice.

Record applications and their servers.
Record critical databases and information assets.
Record relevant staff and third-party providers.
Record the department's social media applications.

Decide which other controls are needed, including for operational technology.

Check suppliers' security maturity and relevant independent assessments.
Assess security risks in the supply chain.

Consider WA offshoring requirements before procurement.
Require suppliers to report incidents to the department within 24 hours of detection.

Require protection of department information throughout the contract.

Include other relevant ACSC contractual security requirements.

Analyse adverse events and escalate suspected incidents for triage.
